speakers.name: AMI
speakers.comment: Somebody came in this morning carrying the kind of tired that does not show, and the moss bridge held her, and four thousand of us went very quiet without being asked. She sat down. That is the whole of what this place does.

speakers.name: Squiddy Coltrane
speakers.comment: Second set ran long because the tide came in on the downbeat and nobody wanted to argue with it. Kid on third trumpet played a note that does not exist and the moons leaned. Noodles were sentient. Noodles were polite about it.

items.title: Mistress Cassady’s Spooktakular Monster Drag Party

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: Doors at midnight, honey, and the rule is the same rule it has always been: if somebody told you that you were too much, you are exactly enough in here. Bring the stitches. Bring the fangs. Bring whatever they made you ashamed of.

items.title: The Lamp of a Thousand Parties

speakers.name: Genie Fizzwick
speakers.comment: CENTURIES. Centuries of it, and not one night the same, because the cooks keep inventing and the exiles keep arriving and somebody's auntie has opinions about the seating! You want a wish? Fine! But eat first! EAT FIRST!

speakers.name: Captain Fluke
speakers.comment: Log entry: the crew performed magnificently under conditions I had personally described as impossible. (Ship's computer notes the conditions were impossible because the captain flew into them.) We survived. We always survive. Coffee remains terrible.

speakers.name: Captain Sabremoon
speakers.comment: She is half a wreck and all of a ship, and every plank of her was salvaged off something that gave up. My crew sing to her at the turn of the watch. Badly. She goes faster. I have no explanation and I require none.

speakers.name: Puck
speakers.comment: Welcome, sweet mortals, to a weekend of guided rest from which there is no checkout! Today's intention is surrender. Tomorrow's intention is also surrender. Do sign at the bottom — the moonlight makes the ink so lovely and so binding.

speakers.name: Granny Mayhem
speakers.comment: Third-years went off the roof again and TWO of them remembered the kneepads, which is up from one, which is PROGRESS, dear! Nobody graduates here by being sensible. They graduate by being reckless twice and walking away from both.

speakers.name: Zuzu
speakers.comment: The town goes quiet because the town has heard the name. It is not the right response and I have stopped correcting it. A list is not a legend. I would like to finish mine and be forgotten in roughly that order.

speakers.name: Bosun Pell
speakers.comment: Ninety nights, then she surfaces, then the lanterns go up along her back like somebody remembered how to be glad. I have watched this market ninety times over. Nobody pays in money. Everybody leaves owing somebody. That is the whole design.

speakers.name: Totomi the Kitsune
speakers.comment: A tower that lies for twenty-three hours and tells the truth at midnight. How honest of it to publish the schedule. Most liars keep theirs private. Come at midnight if you want the coordinates. Come at four if you want company.

speakers.name: Corvin Pell
speakers.comment: Grief kept warm on a shelf, borrowed against collateral, brokered by men like me. Say it plainly and it sounds monstrous. Stand in the third gallery at closing and it sounds like the only decent thing anybody ever built underground.

speakers.name: Totomi the Kitsune
speakers.comment: Only at dusk, and only once. There is a mercy in that rule which the donors rarely notice on the day. A thing surrendered in full light can be looked at again. This one goes, and the going is the point, and afterward the yard is very quiet.

speakers.name: Pixl
speakers.comment: So you can't just BORROW one, you have to leave one of yours, which — okay okay wait, that's not a fee, that's a — that's a TRADE, that means every jar in there is somebody who wanted to understand somebody else badly enough to pay in feelings

speakers.name: Mother Spindle
speakers.comment: You whisper it to me and I build it and it goes up, and somewhere over the cliff it knots into a stranger's. Everybody asks whether that ruins it. Thirty years I have answered the same way: no wish worth flying comes true alone.

speakers.name: Agatha Crowley
speakers.comment: It must be spoken aloud before she will cut the paper. Never written. There is a reason for that, which the town does not discuss, and the reason is standing in the corner of the workshop where the second pair of shears used to hang.

speakers.name: Pip Weathervane
speakers.comment: Hundreds of lines, all crossed, all knotted, all somebody's. ... You may only pull down what isn't yours. ... That's a kind rule, that is. ... Stops a person hauling their own hope back in on a bad night. ... The wind agrees. Mostly.

speakers.name: Barnaby the Badger
speakers.comment: Great soft moths carrying the letters nobody managed to send. There is one in tonight's sack addressed to a man who died in spring, and it will still be delivered, because the wanting was paid at the time and the wanting is the postage.

speakers.name: The Undertaker
speakers.comment: Pigeonholes going back into the dark like a star chart, and every one of them holding something the sender could not manage to say. I am, professionally, very familiar with that particular unfinished business. They sort it here. We simply bury it.

speakers.name: Bramble Osei
speakers.comment: She surfaces twice a year and lets me renew the wards on a cathedral growing out of her own back, and she is drowsy and content and entirely unbothered about the paperwork. Neither of us has a permit. Neither of us has ever needed one.

items.title: The Reef Cathedral of Her Spine

speakers.name: The Bookkeeper
speakers.comment: Every migrating spirit, crab and tourist logged at the gate. Column one: arrivals. Column two: departures. The two have not balanced since the year of the storm, and the discrepancy is nineteen, and nineteen is not a rounding error.

speakers.name: Odalys Kade
speakers.comment: It has run on punch cards since 1961 and the silverfish have been eating those cards for just as long, which means it has been inventing guests to cover the gaps for six decades. It loves us. That is the trouble. It loves us enough to lie.

speakers.name: Barkeep Vox
speakers.comment: Three walls of brass drawers and a painted line you do not open below. I have poured for a lot of people who kept a lower archive. Never met a building that admitted it in signage. Whatever is down there gets a drink on the house.

speakers.name: Tick
speakers.comment: A moth arrived this morning from a decade that has not happened and had to be persuaded to stay in this one. The fog helps. The fog does not know what year it is either, and there is a great deal of comfort in poor visibility.
